title: Pre-clinical study protocol: Blood transfusion in endotoxaemic shock
author: Obonyo, Byrne, et al.

steps.title: Induce sepsis with LPS infusion
steps.instruction: Prepare LPS (E. coli serotype O55:B5) diluted to 0.1 µg ml⁻¹ and infuse via a dose‑escalation schedule to achieve hyperdynamic shock.

substeps.instruction: Infuse at 0.5 µg kg⁻¹ h⁻¹ for 30 min
Increase to 1 µg kg⁻¹ h⁻¹ for 30 min
Increase to 2 µg kg⁻¹ h⁻¹ for 30 min
Increase to 3 µg kg⁻¹ h⁻¹ for 30 min
Maintain at 4 µg kg⁻¹ h⁻¹ for 2 h (total LPS dose = 11.25 µg kg⁻¹)

steps.title: Transfuse packed red blood cells
steps.instruction: Three hours after baseline, administer 10 ml kg⁻¹ of packed red blood cells (ovPRBCs) over 1 h according to the animal’s randomisation group.

steps.title: Monitor animals post‑transfusion
steps.instruction: Observe each animal continuously for 12 h after the transfusion, recording haemodynamic and physiological parameters.

steps.title: Start noradrenaline vasopressor
steps.instruction: If MAP falls below target, begin noradrenaline infusion (60 µg 100 ml⁻¹ in 5 % dextrose) using a Gemini infusion pump, titrating to maintain MAP 60–65 mmHg.

steps.title: Add vasopressin if needed
steps.instruction: If hypotension persists and noradrenaline reaches 20 µg min⁻¹, start vasopressin at 0.8 U h⁻¹ and titrate up to a maximum of 1.6 U h⁻¹ to achieve the MAP target.

steps.title: Euthanize with sodium pentobarbitone
steps.instruction: At the end of the 12‑h monitoring period, inject sodium pentobarbitone intravenously at 162.5 mg kg⁻¹ to euthanise the animal.

steps.title: Perform autopsy and collect tissues
steps.instruction: Conduct a full autopsy, retrieve organ and tissue samples, and store them for subsequent histological analysis.
